description: An enum loses a label while columns, an array column and defaults use it. There is no DROP VALUE: the columns move to a new type, keeping every row.
before: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'paid', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');
after: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');
preserve: SELECT id, s::text, arr::text, s2::text FROM o ORDER BY id

description: An enum's labels are reordered; the type's sort order changes, the rows do not.
before: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'paid', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');
after: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('shipped','paid','new');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');
preserve: SELECT id, s::text, arr::text, s2::text FROM o ORDER BY id

description: An enum gains a label (ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE ... AFTER). Its reverse is a removal.
before: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');
after: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'paid', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');
preserve: SELECT id, s::text, arr::text, s2::text FROM o ORDER BY id

description: A label removal with views, a materialized view, a policy, a trigger condition, a generated column, a partial index, a CHECK, a unique key and a foreign key from another table all using the columns.
before: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'paid', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, s FROM o WHERE s2 IS NOT NULL; CREATE VIEW v2 AS SELECT * FROM v; CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT s FROM o; CREATE INDEX mv_s ON mv (s); ALTER TABLE o ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON o USING (s = 'new'); CREATE FUNCTION tf() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEW; END $$; CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE UPDATE ON o FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.s = 'new') EXECUTE FUNCTION tf(); ALTER TABLE o ADD COLUMN g boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (s = 'new') STORED; CREATE INDEX o_p ON o (id) WHERE s = 'shipped'; ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_ck CHECK (s <> 'shipped' OR s2 IS NOT NULL); ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_u UNIQUE (s, id); CREATE TABLE r (id int, s st, FOREIGN KEY (s, id) REFERENCES o (s, id));
after: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, s FROM o WHERE s2 IS NOT NULL; CREATE VIEW v2 AS SELECT * FROM v; CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT s FROM o; CREATE INDEX mv_s ON mv (s); ALTER TABLE o ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON o USING (s = 'new'); CREATE FUNCTION tf() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEW; END $$; CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE UPDATE ON o FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.s = 'new') EXECUTE FUNCTION tf(); ALTER TABLE o ADD COLUMN g boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (s = 'new') STORED; CREATE INDEX o_p ON o (id) WHERE s = 'shipped'; ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_ck CHECK (s <> 'shipped' OR s2 IS NOT NULL); ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_u UNIQUE (s, id); CREATE TABLE r (id int, s st, FOREIGN KEY (s, id) REFERENCES o (s, id));
preserve: SELECT id, s::text, s2::text FROM o ORDER BY id

description: The same readers, with a label added instead; reverting it is a removal under all of them.
before: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, s FROM o WHERE s2 IS NOT NULL; CREATE VIEW v2 AS SELECT * FROM v; CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT s FROM o; CREATE INDEX mv_s ON mv (s); ALTER TABLE o ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON o USING (s = 'new'); CREATE FUNCTION tf() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEW; END $$; CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE UPDATE ON o FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.s = 'new') EXECUTE FUNCTION tf(); ALTER TABLE o ADD COLUMN g boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (s = 'new') STORED; CREATE INDEX o_p ON o (id) WHERE s = 'shipped'; ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_ck CHECK (s <> 'shipped' OR s2 IS NOT NULL); ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_u UNIQUE (s, id); CREATE TABLE r (id int, s st, FOREIGN KEY (s, id) REFERENCES o (s, id));
after: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'paid', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, s FROM o WHERE s2 IS NOT NULL; CREATE VIEW v2 AS SELECT * FROM v; CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT s FROM o; CREATE INDEX mv_s ON mv (s); ALTER TABLE o ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON o USING (s = 'new'); CREATE FUNCTION tf() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEW; END $$; CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE UPDATE ON o FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.s = 'new') EXECUTE FUNCTION tf(); ALTER TABLE o ADD COLUMN g boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (s = 'new') STORED; CREATE INDEX o_p ON o (id) WHERE s = 'shipped'; ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_ck CHECK (s <> 'shipped' OR s2 IS NOT NULL); ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT o_u UNIQUE (s, id); CREATE TABLE r (id int, s st, FOREIGN KEY (s, id) REFERENCES o (s, id));
preserve: SELECT id, s::text, s2::text FROM o ORDER BY id

description: The label being removed is named by a CHECK and a partial index that go with it; they cannot be put back around the swap.
before: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'paid', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');ALTER TABLE o ADD CONSTRAINT ck_paid CHECK (s <> 'paid'); CREATE INDEX o_paid ON o (id) WHERE s = 'paid';
after: CREATE TYPE st AS ENUM ('new', 'shipped');CREATE TABLE o (id int PRIMARY KEY, s st NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', arr st[] DEFAULT '{new}', s2 st); INSERT INTO o VALUES (1,'new','{new,shipped}','shipped'),(2,'shipped',NULL,'new');

description: GENERATED BY DEFAULT becomes ALWAYS on a column with rows. Dropping and re-adding the identity restarts the sequence and the next insert collides.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: An identity gains INCREMENT BY 10; the sequence keeps its position.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (INCREMENT BY 10) PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: An identity column goes from int to bigint.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: A plain integer key with rows becomes an identity; its sequence must start past the existing values.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int PRIMARY KEY, v int); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,1),(2,2);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: A serial column becomes an identity: its default and owned sequence go, the identity starts past the rows.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id serial PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: An identity becomes a serial column: a sequence owned by it, a nextval default, started past the rows.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id serial PRIMARY KEY, v int);
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: serial becomes bigserial. ALTER COLUMN TYPE does not retype the sequence, which must follow or it still stops at 2^31.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id serial, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id bigserial, v int);INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1,5) g;
preserve: SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id

description: A column gains COMPRESSION lz4 and another STORAGE EXTERNAL.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int, body text, blob bytea);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int, body text COMPRESSION lz4, blob bytea); ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN blob SET STORAGE EXTERNAL;

description: A column is retyped and must keep its storage and compression, which ALTER COLUMN TYPE resets to the new type's defaults.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int, body varchar(200));
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int, body text COMPRESSION lz4); ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN body SET STORAGE EXTERNAL;

description: A stored generated column's expression changes; it can only be dropped and re-added, recomputed.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int primary key, a numeric, g numeric GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a * 2) STORED); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 2);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int primary key, a numeric, g numeric GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a * 3) STORED); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 2);
preserve: SELECT id, a, g FROM t ORDER BY id

description: A plain column becomes a stored generated one.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int, a int, b int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a*2) STORED); INSERT INTO t (id,a) VALUES (1,2);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int, a int, b int); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,2,4);

description: A stored generated column becomes plain (DROP EXPRESSION), keeping its values.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int, a int, b int); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,2,4);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int, a int, b int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a*2) STORED); INSERT INTO t (id,a) VALUES (1,2);

description: Columns retyped (numeric precision, text to uuid) under a security_invoker view with grants and a policy, which PostgreSQL refuses to retype under.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int PRIMARY KEY, a numeric(10,2), uid text); CREATE VIEW v WITH (security_invoker=true) AS SELECT id, a FROM t; GRANT SELECT ON v TO PUBLIC; ALTER TABLE t ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON t USING (uid IS NOT NULL);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int PRIMARY KEY, a numeric(12,2), uid uuid); CREATE VIEW v WITH (security_invoker=true) AS SELECT id, a FROM t; GRANT SELECT ON v TO PUBLIC; ALTER TABLE t ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON t USING (uid IS NOT NULL);

description: A column retyped on a partitioned table read by a view; the partitions follow the parent.
before: CREATE TABLE p (id int, a numeric(10,2)) PARTITION BY RANGE (id); CREATE TABLE p1 PARTITION OF p FOR VALUES FROM (0) TO (100); CREATE VIEW pv AS SELECT a FROM p;
after: CREATE TABLE p (id int, a numeric(12,2)) PARTITION BY RANGE (id); CREATE TABLE p1 PARTITION OF p FOR VALUES FROM (0) TO (100); CREATE VIEW pv AS SELECT a FROM p;

description: A new column typed by a new enum: the type is created first, and dropped last when reverting.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE TYPE e AS ENUM ('a'); CREATE TABLE t (id int, c e);

description: A new column typed by a new domain over a new enum.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE TYPE e AS ENUM ('a'); CREATE DOMAIN d AS e; CREATE TABLE t (id int, c d);

description: A new column defaulting to nextval() of a new sequence.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE SEQUENCE s; CREATE TABLE t (id int DEFAULT nextval('s'));

description: A new column whose default calls a new function: the function must exist first, although functions are otherwise created after tables.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT 7 $$;CREATE TABLE t (id int DEFAULT f());

description: A new CHECK constraint calling a new function.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT 7 $$;CREATE TABLE t (id int CHECK (id < f() * 100));

description: A new expression index calling a new function.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT 7 $$;CREATE TABLE t (id int); CREATE INDEX t_f ON t ((id + f()));

description: A new default calling a new function with arguments, identified by its signature.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE FUNCTION addn(x integer) RETURNS integer LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT x + 1 $$; CREATE TABLE t (id int DEFAULT addn(1));

description: A new trigger with its new trigger function.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int); CREATE FUNCTION tfn() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEW; END $$; CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION tfn();

description: An enum the desired schema no longer has, used by a domain, a column, a function argument and a view: it is dropped last, and recreated first when reverting.
before: CREATE TYPE e AS ENUM ('a','b'); CREATE DOMAIN d AS e; CREATE TABLE t (id int, c e); CREATE FUNCTION fe(x e) RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT 1 $$; CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, c, 'a'::e AS k FROM t;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A sequence and a function used only by defaults of columns that go too.
before: CREATE SEQUENCE s; CREATE FUNCTION g() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT 1 $$; CREATE TABLE t (id int DEFAULT nextval('s'), x int DEFAULT g());
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A table with a view on it, typed by an enum that goes with it.
before: CREATE TYPE e AS ENUM ('a'); CREATE TABLE t (id int); CREATE TABLE t2 (id int, c e); CREATE VIEW v2 AS SELECT * FROM t2;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A SQL function reading a table that goes too; when reverting, the table must be back before the function body is validated.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int); CREATE TABLE t2 (id int); CREATE FUNCTION n() RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT count(*) FROM t2 $$;
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A trigger and its function on a table that goes too.
before: CREATE TABLE t (id int); CREATE TABLE t2 (id int); CREATE FUNCTION tfn() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEW; END $$; CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t2 FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION tfn();
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A column typed by a composite holding an enum; all three go.
before: CREATE TYPE e AS ENUM ('a'); CREATE TYPE c AS (x e, y int); CREATE TABLE t (id int, v c);
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A function used by a CHECK and an expression index that go first.
before: CREATE FUNCTION lim() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT 10 $$; CREATE TABLE t (id int CHECK (id < lim())); CREATE INDEX t_l ON t ((id + lim()));
after: CREATE TABLE t (id int);

description: A foreign key onto a table in another schema, as every Supabase table referencing auth.users has; the reference must keep its schema.
before: CREATE SCHEMA app; CREATE TABLE app.users (id int PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE p (a int, b int, PRIMARY KEY (a, b)); CREATE TABLE profiles (id int, user_id int);
after: CREATE SCHEMA app; CREATE TABLE app.users (id int PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE p (a int, b int, PRIMARY KEY (a, b)); CREATE TABLE profiles (id int, user_id int REFERENCES app.users (id));

description: A foreign key over two columns; the reference must list both.
before: CREATE SCHEMA app; CREATE TABLE app.users (id int PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE p (a int, b int, PRIMARY KEY (a, b)); CREATE TABLE c (x int, y int);
after: CREATE SCHEMA app; CREATE TABLE app.users (id int PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE p (a int, b int, PRIMARY KEY (a, b)); CREATE TABLE c (x int, y int, FOREIGN KEY (x, y) REFERENCES p (a, b));
